note: The promotion rule as DATA, replayed through the implementation. It was restated in six normative places and drifted in all of them. The first version of this file carried only parameters and expectations, and a mutation proved it bound NOTHING: the harness compared the data with itself and never projected anything, so breaking the code left it green. Each case now ships the exact snapshot bytes, receipt bytes and CAS, and the harness projects them. Rows where `record_projected` is false carry no signature nodes at all -- the record was excluded on its own ERR -- so their empty `loss_codes` mean 'nothing to qualify', not 'nothing withheld'.
rule: attribute iff valid && binding == "bound" && grounded; grounded iff grade == "settlement" && trust_config_digest is hex64. Everything weaker emits wrt:claimedSigner with exactly one loss code.

loss_codes.L-UNGROUNDED: binding is bound or unbound while the contract does not require a trust basis
loss_codes.L-UNBOUND: no valid, grounded bound association was established

rule_is_prose: `rule` and `note` are PROSE. The harness does not execute them and cannot: editing this text to say the opposite leaves every case green, which is the same rot that made the profile disagree with the code for four consecutive rounds. The CONTRACT is `cases` — each one carries the exact bytes and the exact expected outcome, and the harness replays them. Read the prose to understand the intent; trust only the cases.
